fact_en:
How often does an asteroid hit Earth?

About once a year, an automobile-sized asteroid hits Earth's atmosphere, but it burns up before reaching the surface!
fact_bis:
Kanus-a kanunay motagbaw ang asteroid sa Earth?

Halos kausa sa usa ka tuig, usa ka asteroid nga sama kadako sa sakyanan ang motagbaw sa atmosphere sa Earth, apan masunog kini sa dili pa makaabot sa yuta!

findings.note: Wrong-sense verb in both title and body. `tagbaw` in Cebuano means SATISFIED/SATED (katagbawan = satisfaction); it is not a verb of collision. title_bis "Pagtagbaw sa Asteroid" reads as "Satisfying the Asteroid" for "Asteroid Impacts", and the body repeats it twice: "Kanus-a kanunay motagbaw ang asteroid sa Earth?" / "...ang motagbaw sa atmosphere sa Earth". The card never uses the correct word anywhere, so the action (an asteroid STRIKING Earth's atmosphere) is never restored. Strong outlier evidence: the sibling cards in this same batch use the correct verb — dcard-05743 "kon ang meteorite MOBANGGA sa usa ka planeta o bulan" and dcard-05744 "kon MOBANGGA ang comet o asteroid". (Secondary, not the flag reason: "Kanus-a kanunay" renders "How often" as "When", though "kausa sa usa ka tuig" partly restores the frequency.)

fact_en: Tephra is fragmented volcanic debris violently ejected into the atmosphere during explosive eruptions, and it can extend tens of kilometers above the volcano.
fact_bis: Ang tephra kay mga tipik nga volcanic debris nga kusganong gipagawas sa atmosphere panahon sa explosive eruptions, ug kini makaabot ug napulo ka mga kilometro sa taas sa bulkan.

findings.note: Tephra height: EN "can extend tens of kilometers above the volcano" becomes "kini makaabot ug napulo ka mga kilometro sa taas sa bulkan" — "napulo ka" is the cardinal TEN, so the Cebuano states a fixed ~10 km instead of the open-ended tens (20-40 km) the English gives. Cebuano for "tens of" is pinulo-pulo / daghang kilometro. Nothing else in the card restores the magnitude, so a child reading only the Cebuano learns a single, smaller number as the height of an eruption column.

fact_en: Bending a glowstick allows two chemicals inside to react and give off light, an example of luminescence.
fact_bis: Ang pagbalik sa glowstick nagtugot sa duha ka kemikal sa sulod nga mo-react ug magpagawas og kahayag, usa ka pananglitan sa luminescence.

findings.note: The action that makes a glowstick work is lost. EN: "BENDING a glowstick allows two chemicals inside to react". BIS: "Ang PAGBALIK sa glowstick nagtugot..." — pagbalik is returning/going back, not bending (bent = baliko, likely a dropped -o). The card is titled "Giunsa Nagtrabaho ang Glowstick", so the trigger action is the fact it depends on, and nothing else on the card names it. Corpus evidence: pagbalik occurs on 75 cards, all meaning return; "bend" is rendered baliko/ibawog/moliko across the corpus, and the sibling glowstick card ffct-04265 says "sama sa pagbaliko sa glow stick aron mosiga". Medium confidence: the chemistry half (two chemicals react, give light, luminescence) does survive.

fact_en: Mimicry is when a harmless animal copies the look, smell, taste, color, or sound of a dangerous animal to protect itself.
fact_bis: Ang mimicry mao ang pag-ila sa usa ka dili peligroso nga mananap sa dagway, baho, lami, kolor, o tingog sa usa ka peligroso nga mananap aron panalipdan ang kaugalingon.

findings.note: Mimicry definition is inverted. EN: "a harmless animal COPIES the look, smell, taste, colour or sound of a dangerous animal". BIS: "Ang mimicry mao ang PAG-ILA sa usa ka dili peligroso nga mananap sa dagway, baho, lami, kolor, o tingog sa usa ka peligroso nga mananap" — pag-ila is to identify/recognise, not to copy. A Cebuano-only child learns that mimicry is the harmless animal RECOGNISING the dangerous one, which is false and is never corrected anywhere on the card (the card has no other verb). Corpus evidence: pag-ila occurs on 74 cards and means identify/recognise on every one; all other mimicry cards use pagsundog/pagpanundog/mokopya (dcard-04237, dcard-12171, dcard-08649, ffct-01226, ffct-08522). Correct word here is pagsundog.

title_bis: Ang Itom Mosuyop, Ang Puti Mopalta
fact_en: Black objects are good absorbers and emitters of radiation, while white or shiny objects reflect more heat and stay cooler under the sun.
fact_bis: Ang mga itom nga butang maayo nga mosuyop ug mopagawas sa radiation, samtang ang puti o sinaw nga butang mas mopalta sa init ug magpabiling mas bugnaw ilalom sa adlaw.

findings.note: title_bis 'Ang Itom Mosuyop, Ang Puti Mopalta' and the body 'ang puti o sinaw nga butang mas mopalta sa init' use 'mopalta' for 'reflect'. Cebuano 'palta' (< Sp. falta) means to be lacking/missing/absent; it is not a word for reflecting light or heat, so the title reads 'Black Absorbs, White Is-Missing' and the card's whole absorb-vs-reflect contrast is never stated. The card never restores it — the only other clue is 'magpabiling mas bugnaw'. Corpus-wide evidence this is an outlier: every other reflection card uses mobalik/magpabalik/gibanda/mobanaag/masalamin/mo-reflect (e.g. ffct-21948 'ang puti nagbalik sa halos tanang kahayag', ffct-22657 'Ang puti nga butang mobalik ug daghang kahayag'), and this batch's own sibling dcard-07181 states the absorber/emitter pair correctly. 'mopalta' occurs in only 4 cards in the entire 337-batch sweep (also dcard-03213, same reflect error).

fact_en: A male butterfly finds a female by detecting a chemical scent she releases, called a pheromone.
fact_bis: Makita sa laki nga butterfly ang baye pinaagi sa pag-detect sa kemikal nga baho nga gipagawas niini, nga gitawag og pheromone.

findings.note: title_bis "Senaryo sa Baho sa Butterfly" for "Butterfly Scent Signal": senaryo = scenario (Sp. escenario), never signal. Cebuano is senyas/senyales, used 86x elsewhere in the corpus (e.g. 'Senyas sa Aninipot', 'Senyas sa Kulay ug Baho'); senaryo appears ONLY here and in dcard-07847. The title names a different thing and the body never uses senyas.

title_bis: Senaryo sa In Heat nga Iring
fact_en: A cat in heat makes more noise, meows louder and more often, and becomes very affectionate toward people.
fact_bis: Ang iring nga in heat mas saba, mas kusog ug mas kanunay nga mo-meow, ug mahimo nga hilabihan ka affectionate sa mga tawo.

findings.note: title_bis "Senaryo sa In Heat nga Iring" for "Cat Heat Signs": same defect as dcard-07838 — senaryo (scenario) substituted for senyales (signs). Corpus convention is senyas/senyales; these two cards are the only senaryo hits in the whole sweep. Body describes the signs but never names them senyales.

title_bis: Batas sa Iring nga In Heat
fact_en: A cat in heat weaves in and out of people's legs, rubs against them, shakes her pelvis, rolls on the floor, and flags her tail.
fact_bis: Ang iring nga in heat mosulod-gawas sa mga batiis sa mga tawo, mokuskos kanila, mag-uyog sa iyang pelvis, magligid sa salog, ug mag-flag sa iyang ikog.

findings.note: title_bis "Batas sa Iring nga In Heat" for "Cat Heat Behavior": batas is the law word (the corpus itself uses Batas/Balaod ni Newton, Boyle, Ohm, Charles ~20x for LAW), so the title reads "Law of the cat in heat". Cebuano for behavior is batasan / kinaiya / panggawi, which the corpus uses elsewhere ("Maayong Batasan", "Daotang Batasan"). The body lists the behaviors but never supplies the right head-word.

fact_en: During carbon fixation, carbon dioxide from the air is attached to a five-carbon molecule called RuDP, creating an unstable six-carbon molecule that immediately splits into two PGA molecules.
fact_bis: Sa carbon fixation, ang carbon dioxide sa hangin ikabit sa usa ka five-carbon molecule nga gitawag ug RuDP, nga maghimo ug dili lig-on nga six-carbon molecule nga dayon matunga sa duha ka PGA molecules.

findings.note: title_bis "Pag-ayo sa Carbon Dioxide" for "Fixing Carbon Dioxide": pag-ayo = to repair/heal, so the title claims CO2 is being repaired. The card's OWN body keeps the correct term ("Sa carbon fixation, ang carbon dioxide sa hangin ikabit sa ... RuDP"), and the rest of the corpus leaves the term in English (dcard-03363 'Carbon Fixation', dcard-07991 'Ang Enzyme sa Carbon Fixation'), so the title is the outlier. Should be "Carbon Fixation" / "Pagkabit sa Carbon Dioxide".

fact_en: Most PGAL molecules are used to regenerate RuDP, the starting molecule, so the Calvin cycle can keep turning and fix more carbon dioxide.
fact_bis: Kadaghanan sa mga PGAL molecules gamiton aron ma-regenerate ang RuDP, ang sinugdanan nga molecule, aron magpadayon ang pagtuyok sa Calvin cycle ug maka-ayo pa ug mas daghang carbon dioxide.

findings.note: bis body: "...aron magpadayon ang pagtuyok sa Calvin cycle ug maka-ayo pa ug mas daghang carbon dioxide" for "...so the Calvin cycle can keep turning and fix more carbon dioxide" — maka-ayo = can repair/heal, so the card says the cycle heals CO2. Nothing in the card restores the fixation sense (the correct term 'carbon fixation' appears only on sibling cards, not this one). Same wrong-sense verb as dcard-07990.

fact_en:
How can you compare two things at once?

A Venn diagram uses overlapping circles to show what is similar and what is different between two sets!
fact_bis:
Unsaon nimo pagtandi ang duha ka butang sa usa ka higayon?

Ang Venn diagram mogamit ug magkatapad nga mga lingin aron ipakita kung unsa ang pareho ug unsa ang lahi sa duha ka set!

findings.note: Venn diagram: English "overlapping circles" becomes "magkatapad nga mga lingin" = circles placed BESIDE each other / adjacent. Cebuano for overlapping is nagsapaw / nagpatong-patong (or nag-overlap). The overlap IS the mechanism the card teaches — a child following the Cebuano draws two side-by-side circles and has nowhere to put "unsa ang pareho", so the fact is unrecoverable from the card; nothing else in the body or title restores it (title_bis is just "Venn Diagram", and the English term 'overlapping circles' survives only in the untranslated `terms` list, which the child does not read).

fact_en: Animals move in different ways depending on their habitat and body structure - some walk, hop, jump, fly, crawl, or swim.
fact_bis: Lainlain ang paagi sa paglihok sa mga mananap depende sa ilang habitat ug istruktura sa lawas - ang uban molakaw, molukso, motipdas, molupad, mokamang, o molangoy.

findings.note: Animal Movements. EN lists "walk, hop, jump, fly, crawl, or swim"; bis renders it "molakaw, molukso, motipdas, molupad, mokamang, o molangoy". `tipdas` is Cebuano for MEASLES (Tagalog tigdas) — confirmed by the rest of this corpus, where all 220 other occurrences of the word are the disease ("bakunang MMR ... batok sa tulo ka sakit: tipdas, beke, ug rubella"); the verbed form `motipdas` occurs nowhere else except this one card. The Cebuano word for jump is molukso/moambak. A child reading only the Cebuano gets a disease word inside a list of ways animals move, and the "jump" item is never restored anywhere else on the card.
